name: P1 · Health Education
description: 8 of 10 topics so far (16 sets × 20 questions): Health Education – Basics; Health and Diseases; Non-Communicable & Lifestyle Diseases; Mental Health; Food for Healthy Living; Reproductive Health; Growing with Self-Confidence; Social Health. More topics are added to this pack as the plan goes on; re-importing only adds the new sets.

sets.name: 1 · Health Education: Meaning, Definition and Importance

questions.question: According to the WHO (1948), health is:

options.B: A state of complete physical, mental and social well-being and not merely the absence of disease or infirmity

questions.subject: Health Education: Meaning, Definition and Importance
questions.explanation: This definition is in the Preamble to the WHO Constitution.

questions.question: World Health Day is observed every year on:
questions.subject: Health Education: Meaning, Definition and Importance
questions.explanation: It marks the founding of the WHO in 1948. 1 Dec – World AIDS Day; 5 June – Environment Day; 21 June – Yoga Day.

questions.question: The headquarters of the World Health Organization is at:
questions.subject: Health Education: Meaning, Definition and Importance
questions.explanation: WHO is a specialised agency of the United Nations.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the commonly stated dimensions of health?
questions.subject: Health Education: Meaning, Definition and Importance
questions.explanation: Physical, mental, social (and also spiritual and emotional) dimensions are discussed.

questions.question: Health education is best described as:

options.D: A process of learning experiences that helps people adopt behaviour which promotes health

questions.subject: Health Education: Meaning, Definition and Importance
questions.explanation: Its focus is on knowledge, attitudes and practices (KAP).

questions.question: The three components commonly aimed at by health education are summed up as:
questions.subject: Health Education: Meaning, Definition and Importance
questions.explanation: Knowing is not enough; attitudes and habits must change.

questions.question: 'Health education is the translation of what is known about health into desirable individual and community behaviour patterns by means of the educational process.' This definition is by:
questions.subject: Health Education: Meaning, Definition and Importance
questions.explanation: Grout's definition is widely quoted in health education texts.

questions.question: Which principle of health education says teaching should start from what people already know?

options.A: Proceeding from the known to the unknown

questions.subject: Health Education: Meaning, Definition and Importance
questions.explanation: Other principles include interest, participation, motivation, comprehension, reinforcement and learning by doing.

questions.question: A health message is more likely to change behaviour when the people take an active part in discussions and activities. This is the principle of:
questions.subject: Health Education: Meaning, Definition and Importance
questions.explanation: Active participation leads to acceptance of new health habits.

questions.question: The Alma-Ata Declaration (1978) is associated with:

options.D: Primary health care and the goal 'Health for All by 2000'

questions.subject: Health Education: Meaning, Definition and Importance
questions.explanation: It made primary health care the key to health for all.

questions.question: The three main components of a school health programme are:

options.A: School health services, a healthful school environment and health instruction
options.B: Sports day, annual day and tours

questions.subject: Health Education: Meaning, Definition and Importance
questions.explanation: Health education in schools covers all three.

questions.question: Health education is important mainly because:

options.A: It guarantees that nobody falls ill
options.B: Prevention of disease is easier and cheaper than cure
options.D: It is required only for sick people

questions.subject: Health Education: Meaning, Definition and Importance
questions.explanation: Healthy habits prevent many diseases.

questions.question: A teacher displays charts on hand-washing, demonstrates the steps and asks pupils to practise daily. The teacher is applying the principle of:
questions.subject: Health Education: Meaning, Definition and Importance
questions.explanation: Practice turns knowledge into habit.

questions.question:
Match the day with its date:
a. World Health Day
b. World AIDS Day
c. International Day of Yoga
d. World No Tobacco Day

1. 31 May
2. 7 April
3. 1 December
4. 21 June
questions.subject: Health Education: Meaning, Definition and Importance
questions.explanation: These days are used for health awareness campaigns.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. Health includes mental and social well-being, not only physical fitness.
II. A person without any disease is always completely healthy according to the WHO.
Which is/are correct?
questions.subject: Health Education: Meaning, Definition and Importance
questions.explanation: The WHO definition says health is not merely the absence of disease.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. Health education aims at changing health behaviour, not only giving information.
II. Health education is useful for healthy people as well as sick people.
Which is/are correct?
questions.subject: Health Education: Meaning, Definition and Importance
questions.explanation: Both are central ideas of health education.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Health education gives importance to changing attitudes and habits.
Reason (R): Knowledge alone does not always lead people to adopt healthy practices.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Health Education: Meaning, Definition and Importance
questions.explanation: Many people know that smoking is harmful and still smoke.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Health education is needed only after a disease has broken out.
Reason (R): Health education aims at the prevention of disease.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Health Education: Meaning, Definition and Importance
questions.explanation: Because its aim is prevention, it is needed before diseases occur; R shows why A is false.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): The WHO was established in 1948.
Reason (R): The WHO's definition of health includes social well-being.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Health Education: Meaning, Definition and Importance
questions.explanation: Both true, but unrelated.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Health education in schools can influence the health of the whole community.
Reason (R): Children carry health habits and messages to their families.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Health Education: Meaning, Definition and Importance
questions.explanation: Pupils act as agents of change at home.

questions.question: The word 'hygiene' comes from Hygieia, who in Greek mythology was the goddess of:
questions.subject: Personal Health and Hygiene
questions.explanation: Hygiene is the science and practice of preserving health.

questions.question: Personal hygiene refers to:

options.B: Keeping one's own body, clothes and surroundings clean to stay healthy

questions.subject: Personal Health and Hygiene
questions.explanation: It includes care of skin, hair, teeth, nails, eyes, ears and clothes.

questions.question: Health agencies recommend washing hands with soap and water for at least:
questions.subject: Personal Health and Hygiene
questions.explanation: Scrubbing all parts of the hands for about 20 seconds removes most germs.

questions.question: Global Handwashing Day is observed on:
questions.subject: Personal Health and Hygiene
questions.explanation: It promotes hand-washing with soap to prevent diarrhoea and respiratory infections.

questions.question: Which disease is spread mainly by the faeco-oral route and is prevented by hand-washing and safe water?
questions.subject: Personal Health and Hygiene
questions.explanation: Malaria and dengue are spread by mosquitoes; tetanus enters through wounds.

questions.question: Keeping fingernails short and clean helps mainly to prevent:

options.C: Worm infestation and other faeco-oral infections

questions.subject: Personal Health and Hygiene
questions.explanation: Worm eggs and germs collect under long nails and reach the mouth.

questions.question: Dental experts advise brushing the teeth:

options.A: At least twice a day, especially at night before sleeping

questions.subject: Personal Health and Hygiene
questions.explanation: Brushing removes plaque that causes dental caries and gum disease.

questions.question: Scabies, an itchy skin disease that spreads by close contact, is caused by a:
questions.subject: Personal Health and Hygiene
questions.explanation: Personal cleanliness and not sharing clothes help prevent it.

questions.question: Head lice infestation (pediculosis) is best prevented by:

options.D: Keeping hair clean and not sharing combs, caps and towels

questions.subject: Personal Health and Hygiene
questions.explanation: Lice spread through close contact and shared personal items.

questions.question: The '20-20-20 rule' for people who use screens for long hours means:

options.C: Every 20 minutes, look at something about 20 feet away for 20 seconds
options.D: Use the screen only for 20 minutes a day

questions.subject: Personal Health and Hygiene
questions.explanation: It relaxes the eye muscles and reduces eye strain.

questions.question: According to the WHO, children and adolescents aged 5–17 years should do moderate-to-vigorous physical activity of, on average, at least:
questions.subject: Personal Health and Hygiene
questions.explanation: Regular activity builds fitness and healthy bones and muscles.

questions.question: Adolescents (13–18 years) are generally advised to sleep about:
questions.subject: Personal Health and Hygiene
questions.explanation: Adequate sleep supports growth, memory and attention.

questions.question: Which practice is harmful to the ears?

options.A: Inserting sharp objects such as pins to clean them
options.D: Cleaning the outer ear with a soft cloth

questions.subject: Personal Health and Hygiene
questions.explanation: Sharp objects can damage the ear drum.

questions.question: Which of the following is a good food-hygiene practice?

options.A: Keeping cooked food in the sun
options.B: Using the same knife for raw meat and salad without washing
options.C: Washing fruits and vegetables before eating and keeping food covered
options.D: Eating food left uncovered on the roadside

questions.subject: Personal Health and Hygiene
questions.explanation: Covering food prevents flies and dust from contaminating it.

questions.question:
Match the body part with a hygiene practice:
a. Teeth
b. Eyes
c. Skin
d. Hair

1. Brushing twice daily
2. Regular washing and combing
3. Washing with clean water and resting them
4. Daily bathing
questions.subject: Personal Health and Hygiene
questions.explanation: Each part of the body needs its own care.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. Sharing towels and combs can spread skin infections and lice.
II. Good posture while sitting and standing is part of personal health.
Which is/are correct?
questions.subject: Personal Health and Hygiene
questions.explanation: Both are aspects of personal health and hygiene.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. Drinking boiled or purified water helps prevent diarrhoea and cholera.
II. Washing hands only with water is as effective as washing with soap.
Which is/are correct?
questions.subject: Personal Health and Hygiene
questions.explanation: Soap removes germs and grease much better than water alone.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Washing hands with soap reduces diarrhoeal diseases.
Reason (R): Many diarrhoea-causing germs reach the mouth through dirty hands.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Personal Health and Hygiene
questions.explanation: Hand-washing breaks the faeco-oral route of transmission.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Personal hygiene is important for good health.
Reason (R): Hygieia was the Greek goddess of health.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Personal Health and Hygiene
questions.explanation: Both true, but the origin of the word does not explain why hygiene matters.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Long nails are good for health because they protect the fingers.
Reason (R): Dirt and worm eggs can collect under long nails.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Personal Health and Hygiene
questions.explanation: Because dirt and eggs collect under them, long nails are unhygienic; R shows why A is false.

questions.question: In India's public health system, primary health care is provided mainly through:
questions.subject: Health and Health Systems
questions.explanation: Community Health Centres and district hospitals form the secondary level; medical colleges the tertiary level.

questions.question: Arrange the levels of health care in India from the first contact point upwards:

options.A: CHC → sub-centre → PHC → medical college → district hospital
options.C: Sub-centre → PHC → CHC → district hospital → medical college/tertiary hospital

questions.subject: Health and Health Systems
questions.explanation: Patients are referred upwards when more specialised care is needed.

questions.question: Under the Indian Public Health Standards, a sub-centre in the plains serves a population of about:
questions.subject: Health and Health Systems
questions.explanation: A PHC serves about 30,000 (20,000 in hilly/tribal areas) and a CHC about 1,20,000 (80,000).

questions.question: ASHA, the community health worker under the National Rural Health Mission, stands for:
questions.subject: Health and Health Systems
questions.explanation: There is roughly one ASHA per 1,000 rural population.

questions.question: The National Health Mission has two sub-missions:

options.C: National Rural Health Mission (2005) and National Urban Health Mission (2013)

questions.subject: Health and Health Systems
questions.explanation: Both aim to strengthen public health systems.

questions.question: Ayushman Bharat (2018) has two components:

options.D: Health and Wellness Centres (now Ayushman Arogya Mandirs) and the Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PM-JAY) health insurance

questions.subject: Health and Health Systems
questions.explanation: PM-JAY provides hospital cover of up to ₹5 lakh per family per year.

questions.question: Janani Suraksha Yojana promotes:

options.A: Institutional deliveries by giving cash assistance to pregnant women

questions.subject: Health and Health Systems
questions.explanation: It aims to reduce maternal and newborn deaths.

questions.question: Mission Indradhanush (2014) aims to:

options.A: Increase full immunisation coverage of children and pregnant women

questions.subject: Health and Health Systems
questions.explanation: It strengthens the Universal Immunisation Programme.

questions.question:
Match the level of prevention with an example:
a. Primary prevention
b. Secondary prevention
c. Tertiary prevention
d. Primordial prevention

1. Immunisation against measles
2. Promoting healthy lifestyles in children before risk factors appear
3. Screening to detect breast cancer early
4. Physiotherapy and rehabilitation after a stroke
questions.subject: Health and Health Systems
questions.explanation: Primary prevention acts before disease occurs; secondary detects it early; tertiary limits disability.

questions.question: Vaccination is an example of which kind of prevention?
questions.subject: Health and Health Systems
questions.explanation: It prevents the disease from occurring at all.

questions.question: The Infant Mortality Rate (IMR) is the number of deaths of infants under one year of age per:
questions.subject: Health and Health Systems
questions.explanation: The Maternal Mortality Ratio is expressed per 1,00,000 live births.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT usually listed as a determinant of health?

options.A: Income, education and access to health services

questions.subject: Health and Health Systems
questions.explanation: Behaviour and lifestyle are also important determinants.

questions.question: An essential principle of primary health care is:

options.A: Care only in big city hospitals
options.B: Community participation and equitable distribution of services
options.C: Use of the most expensive technology

questions.subject: Health and Health Systems
questions.explanation: Inter-sectoral coordination and appropriate technology are other principles.

questions.question: The Universal Immunisation Programme of India was launched in:
questions.subject: Health and Health Systems
questions.explanation: It provides free vaccines against several childhood diseases.

questions.question: In India, the telephone number 108 is widely used for:
questions.subject: Health and Health Systems
questions.explanation: Many states, including Karnataka, run 108 emergency ambulance services.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. A Community Health Centre is a referral unit for several PHCs.
II. A sub-centre is headed by a specialist surgeon.
Which is/are correct?
questions.subject: Health and Health Systems
questions.explanation: Sub-centres are run by health workers (ANM and male health worker).

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. Screening tests are a form of secondary prevention.
II. Rehabilitation is a form of tertiary prevention.
Which is/are correct?
questions.subject: Health and Health Systems
questions.explanation: Both statements are correct.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Prevention is given great importance in public health.
Reason (R): Preventing disease is usually easier and cheaper than treating it.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Health and Health Systems
questions.explanation: It saves lives and money.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Primary health care depends only on doctors in city hospitals.
Reason (R): Primary health care stresses community participation and services close to where people live.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Health and Health Systems
questions.explanation: R describes primary health care correctly, which shows that A is false.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): ASHAs work at the village level.
Reason (R): The Universal Immunisation Programme began in 1985.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Health and Health Systems
questions.explanation: Both true but unrelated.

sets.name: 2 · Infectious Diseases: Causes, Symptoms, Transmission, Prevention and Control

questions.question: An infectious (communicable) disease is one that:

options.B: Is caused by a pathogen and can spread from one person or animal to another
options.D: Is caused only by poor diet

questions.subject: Infectious Diseases: Causes, Symptoms, Transmission, Prevention and Control
questions.explanation: Pathogens include viruses, bacteria, protozoa, fungi and worms.

questions.question: The time between the entry of a pathogen into the body and the appearance of the first symptoms is called the:
questions.subject: Infectious Diseases: Causes, Symptoms, Transmission, Prevention and Control
questions.explanation: It differs from disease to disease.

questions.question:
Match the disease with its main mode of transmission:
a. Tuberculosis
b. Cholera
c. Dengue
d. Hepatitis B

1. Bite of an Aedes mosquito
2. Airborne droplets
3. Infected blood and body fluids
4. Contaminated water and food
questions.subject: Infectious Diseases: Causes, Symptoms, Transmission, Prevention and Control
questions.explanation: Knowing the route of spread tells us how to prevent the disease.

questions.question:
Match the mosquito with a disease it spreads:
a. Anopheles
b. Aedes
c. Culex

1. Dengue and chikungunya
2. Filariasis (elephantiasis)
3. Malaria
questions.subject: Infectious Diseases: Causes, Symptoms, Transmission, Prevention and Control
questions.explanation: Only female mosquitoes bite and spread these diseases.

questions.question: The Aedes aegypti mosquito, which spreads dengue, mainly:

options.A: Bites only at midnight and breeds in sewage
options.D: Bites during the day and breeds in clean stored water in containers, coolers and tyres

questions.subject: Infectious Diseases: Causes, Symptoms, Transmission, Prevention and Control
questions.explanation: Removing stagnant water around homes is the key to prevention.

questions.question: A cough lasting more than two weeks, with fever and weight loss, is a typical warning sign of:
questions.subject: Infectious Diseases: Causes, Symptoms, Transmission, Prevention and Control
questions.explanation: TB is caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis; the BCG vaccine protects children against severe forms.

questions.question: 'Rice-water' stools with severe dehydration are characteristic of:
questions.subject: Infectious Diseases: Causes, Symptoms, Transmission, Prevention and Control
questions.explanation: Cholera is caused by Vibrio cholerae; oral rehydration is life-saving.

questions.question: Oral Rehydration Solution (ORS) is given in diarrhoea mainly to:

options.C: Replace the water and salts lost from the body

questions.subject: Infectious Diseases: Causes, Symptoms, Transmission, Prevention and Control
questions.explanation: Zinc supplements are also given to children with diarrhoea.

questions.question: Typhoid fever is caused by:

options.C: Salmonella Typhi, spread through contaminated food and water

questions.subject: Infectious Diseases: Causes, Symptoms, Transmission, Prevention and Control
questions.explanation: The Widal test is a traditional blood test used in diagnosis.

questions.question: After a dog bite, the correct first-aid step is to:

options.B: Bandage it tightly and ignore it
options.D: Wash the wound thoroughly with soap and running water for about 15 minutes and get anti-rabies vaccination promptly

questions.subject: Infectious Diseases: Causes, Symptoms, Transmission, Prevention and Control
questions.explanation: Rabies is almost always fatal once symptoms appear, so treatment must start early.

questions.question: Tetanus is caused by bacteria that usually enter the body through:

options.B: Wounds contaminated with soil, dust or rusty objects

questions.subject: Infectious Diseases: Causes, Symptoms, Transmission, Prevention and Control
questions.explanation: It is prevented by tetanus toxoid (Td) vaccination.

questions.question: Which pair of diseases is spread mainly by the faeco-oral route (contaminated food and water)?
questions.subject: Infectious Diseases: Causes, Symptoms, Transmission, Prevention and Control
questions.explanation: Hepatitis B and C spread through blood and body fluids.

questions.question: Measles is caused by a ______ and is prevented by the ______ vaccine.
questions.subject: Infectious Diseases: Causes, Symptoms, Transmission, Prevention and Control
questions.explanation: Measles causes fever, cough and a spreading rash.

questions.question: The correct order of the 'chain of infection' is:

options.A: Transmission → agent → host → reservoir → entry → exit
options.B: Host → agent → reservoir → exit → entry → transmission
options.C: Infectious agent → reservoir → portal of exit → mode of transmission → portal of entry → susceptible host
options.D: Reservoir → host → agent → transmission → exit → entry

questions.subject: Infectious Diseases: Causes, Symptoms, Transmission, Prevention and Control
questions.explanation: Breaking any one link stops the spread of the disease.

questions.question: Isolation and quarantine differ in that:

options.D: Isolation separates people who are sick; quarantine restricts healthy people who may have been exposed

questions.subject: Infectious Diseases: Causes, Symptoms, Transmission, Prevention and Control
questions.explanation: Both limit the spread of infection.

questions.question: Immunity produced by a vaccine is:
questions.subject: Infectious Diseases: Causes, Symptoms, Transmission, Prevention and Control
questions.explanation: Antibodies passed from mother to baby give naturally acquired passive immunity.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. Antibiotics are effective against bacterial infections.
II. Using mosquito nets and removing stagnant water helps prevent malaria.
Which is/are correct?
questions.subject: Infectious Diseases: Causes, Symptoms, Transmission, Prevention and Control
questions.explanation: Both are correct; antibiotics do not act on viruses.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. HIV spreads through shaking hands and sharing food.
II. Tuberculosis spreads through droplets when an infected person coughs or sneezes.
Which is/are correct?
questions.subject: Infectious Diseases: Causes, Symptoms, Transmission, Prevention and Control
questions.explanation: HIV does not spread through casual contact; it spreads through blood, sexual contact and from mother to child.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Hand-washing and safe drinking water reduce cholera and typhoid.
Reason (R): These diseases spread mainly through contaminated food and water.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Infectious Diseases: Causes, Symptoms, Transmission, Prevention and Control
questions.explanation: Breaking the faeco-oral route prevents them.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Dengue can be prevented by taking antibiotics.
Reason (R): Dengue is caused by a virus.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Infectious Diseases: Causes, Symptoms, Transmission, Prevention and Control
questions.explanation: Antibiotics do not act on viruses, so A is false; prevention relies on mosquito control.

questions.question: Non-communicable diseases (NCDs) are diseases that:

options.C: Are not passed from person to person and usually last a long time

questions.subject: Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.explanation: They are also called chronic diseases.

questions.question: According to the WHO, the four main groups of NCDs are:

options.A: Cardiovascular diseases, cancers, chronic respiratory diseases and diabetes

questions.subject: Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KPSC / KEA / SSC). Together they cause most NCD deaths.

questions.question: According to the WHO, NCDs cause about what share of all deaths worldwide?
questions.subject: Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.explanation: About 41 million deaths a year.

questions.question: The four main modifiable behavioural risk factors for NCDs are:

options.C: Age, sex, height and blood group
options.D: Tobacco use, physical inactivity, harmful use of alcohol and unhealthy diet

questions.subject: Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KPSC / KEA / SSC). Changing these behaviours prevents much NCD illness.

questions.question: Insulin is produced by the:

options.C: Beta cells of the islets of Langerhans in the pancreas

questions.subject: Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KPSC / KEA / SSC). It lowers blood glucose.

questions.question: Type 1 diabetes is caused mainly by:

options.A: The body's immune system destroying insulin-producing cells, so little or no insulin is made
options.D: Eating too much sugar in one day

questions.subject: Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KPSC / KEA / SSC). Type 2 diabetes involves insulin resistance and is strongly linked to lifestyle.

questions.question: A fasting plasma glucose level of how much or above indicates diabetes?
questions.subject: Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.explanation: 100–125 mg/dL is 'prediabetes' (impaired fasting glucose).

questions.question: Hypertension is generally diagnosed when blood pressure is persistently at or above:
questions.subject: Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KPSC / KEA / SSC). Around 120/80 mmHg is considered normal.

questions.question: Hypertension is often called the 'silent killer' because:

options.A: It makes no sound in a stethoscope
options.B: It is always fatal within days
options.D: It usually causes no symptoms while damaging the heart, brain and kidneys

questions.subject: Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.explanation: Regular checking is the only way to detect it early.

questions.question: A cancer that spreads from its original site to other parts of the body is said to have:
questions.subject: Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.explanation: Malignant tumours can metastasise; benign ones do not.

questions.question: Chewing tobacco is a major cause of which cancer in India?
questions.subject: Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.explanation: India bears a large share of the world's oral-cancer cases.

questions.question: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is caused mainly by:

options.A: Smoking and long exposure to smoke and dust

questions.subject: Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.explanation: It makes breathing progressively harder.

questions.question: World Diabetes Day is observed on:
questions.subject: Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KPSC / KEA / SSC). It is the birthday of Frederick Banting, co-discoverer of insulin.

questions.question: World Cancer Day is observed on:
questions.subject: Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KPSC / KEA / SSC). It is led by the Union for International Cancer Control.

questions.question: World Heart Day is observed on:
questions.subject: Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.explanation: It is promoted by the World Heart Federation.

questions.question: India's national programme for prevention and control of cancer, diabetes, cardiovascular diseases and stroke, launched in 2010, was abbreviated as:
questions.subject: Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KPSC / KEA / SSC). It has since been renamed the National Programme for Prevention and Control of Non-Communicable Diseases (NP-NCD).

questions.question:
Match the NCD with the organ mainly affected:
a. Diabetes
b. Hypertension
c. COPD
d. Stroke

1. Blood vessels and heart
2. Brain
3. Pancreas (insulin) and blood sugar control
4. Lungs
questions.subject: Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.explanation: NCDs affect different organ systems.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. Diabetes can be caught from a diabetic person.
II. Regular screening helps detect hypertension early.

questions.explanation: Diabetes is non-communicable.

questions.subject: Non-Communicable Diseases

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Type 1 diabetes is caused mainly by overeating sweets.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A

options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Non-Communicable Diseases

questions.question: Lifestyle diseases are diseases that are caused or made worse mainly by:

options.D: Daily habits such as diet, physical activity, smoking and stress

questions.subject: Lifestyle Diseases: Causes and Prevention

questions.question: Body Mass Index (BMI) is calculated as:
questions.subject: Lifestyle Diseases: Causes and Prevention
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KPSC / KEA / SSC). It is a simple screening measure of body weight.

questions.subject: Lifestyle Diseases: Causes and Prevention

questions.subject: Lifestyle Diseases: Causes and Prevention

questions.question: By the WHO's international classification, a BMI of 18.5–24.9 is:
questions.subject: Lifestyle Diseases: Causes and Prevention

questions.question: The WHO recommends that adults do at least how much moderate-intensity physical activity per week?
questions.subject: Lifestyle Diseases: Causes and Prevention
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KPSC / KEA / SSC). Or 75 minutes of vigorous activity.

questions.question: The WHO recommends that adults consume less than how much salt per day?
questions.subject: Lifestyle Diseases: Causes and Prevention

questions.question: Atherosclerosis is:

questions.subject: Lifestyle Diseases: Causes and Prevention
questions.explanation: It can lead to heart attacks and strokes.

questions.question: A heart attack (myocardial infarction) occurs when:

options.A: Blood flow in a coronary artery is blocked and heart muscle is damaged

questions.subject: Lifestyle Diseases: Causes and Prevention
questions.explanation: Chest pain spreading to the arm or jaw is a warning sign.

questions.question: A stroke occurs when:

options.C: The blood supply to part of the brain is interrupted or a blood vessel in the brain bursts
options.D: The heart beats too slowly for a moment

questions.subject: Lifestyle Diseases: Causes and Prevention
questions.explanation: Sudden weakness of one side of the body or slurred speech are signs.

questions.question: Which habit most increases the risk of lifestyle diseases?

options.D: Sitting for long hours with little physical activity

questions.subject: Lifestyle Diseases: Causes and Prevention
questions.explanation: A sedentary lifestyle contributes to obesity, diabetes and heart disease.

questions.question: Trans fats, found in some fried and bakery foods made with partially hydrogenated oils, are harmful mainly because they:

options.A: Raise 'bad' LDL cholesterol and lower 'good' HDL cholesterol

questions.subject: Lifestyle Diseases: Causes and Prevention
questions.explanation: The WHO has called for their elimination from the food supply.

questions.question: Adults are generally advised to sleep about:
questions.subject: Lifestyle Diseases: Causes and Prevention
questions.explanation: Poor sleep is linked to obesity, diabetes and heart disease.

questions.question: The Fit India Movement was launched on National Sports Day, 29 August:
questions.subject: Lifestyle Diseases: Causes and Prevention
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KPSC / KEA / SSC). National Sports Day marks the birth anniversary of Major Dhyan Chand.

questions.question: International Day of Yoga is observed on:
questions.subject: Lifestyle Diseases: Causes and Prevention
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KPSC / KEA / SSC). It was first observed in 2015 after a UN General Assembly resolution in 2014.

questions.question: The 'Eat Right India' movement, promoting safe, healthy and sustainable food, is led by:

options.A: FSSAI (Food Safety and Standards Authority of India)

questions.subject: Lifestyle Diseases: Causes and Prevention
questions.explanation: It was launched in 2018.

questions.question:
Match the lifestyle factor with the disease it most directly raises the risk of:

d. Excess alcohol

1. Type 2 diabetes
2. Hypertension
3. Liver cirrhosis
4. Lung cancer
questions.subject: Lifestyle Diseases: Causes and Prevention
questions.explanation: Each habit targets particular organs.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. Regular exercise helps control blood sugar and blood pressure.
II. Yoga and meditation can help manage stress.
Which is/are correct?
questions.subject: Lifestyle Diseases: Causes and Prevention
questions.explanation: Both are correct.

questions.question:

questions.subject: Lifestyle Diseases: Causes and Prevention

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A

sets.name: 1 · Meaning, Characteristics, Stress and Defence Mechanisms

questions.question:
Identify the correct statements regarding mental health:
I. It involves a state of being free from psychological disorders.
II. It involves a state of emotional well-being.
III. It requires the ability to cope with stress.
IV. It is influenced by social and environmental factors.
V. It is merely an absence of mental illness.

options.C: I, II, III and IV only

questions.subject: Meaning, Characteristics, Stress and Defence Mechanisms
questions.explanation: Mental health is a positive state of well-being, not merely the absence of illness, so V is wrong. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: WHO describes mental health as a state of well-being in which a person:

options.B: Realises his or her abilities, can cope with the normal stresses of life, can work productively and contributes to the community
options.D: Is free from all physical disease

questions.subject: Meaning, Characteristics, Stress and Defence Mechanisms
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KPSC / KEA / TET). It is more than the absence of mental disorder.

questions.question: According to the WHO Constitution (1948), health is:

options.A: A state of complete physical, mental and social well-being and not merely the absence of disease or infirmity

questions.subject: Meaning, Characteristics, Stress and Defence Mechanisms
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KPSC / KEA / TET). One of the most frequently asked definitions.

questions.question: The mental hygiene movement was started by Clifford Beers, whose book about his own illness was:
questions.subject: Meaning, Characteristics, Stress and Defence Mechanisms
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KPSC / KEA / TET). Mental hygiene aims at preserving mental health and preventing mental disorders.

questions.question: Which is a characteristic of a mentally healthy person?

options.A: Depends entirely on others for decisions
options.C: Is never anxious in any situation
options.D: Accepts himself and others, sees reality as it is, and adjusts to changing situations

questions.subject: Meaning, Characteristics, Stress and Defence Mechanisms
questions.explanation: Emotional maturity and good relationships are other signs.

questions.question: In psychology, 'adjustment' means:

options.B: A harmonious relationship between a person's needs and the demands of the environment

questions.subject: Meaning, Characteristics, Stress and Defence Mechanisms
questions.explanation: Maladjustment shows up as anxiety, aggression or withdrawal.

questions.question: The 'General Adaptation Syndrome' of stress, with the stages alarm, resistance and exhaustion, was described by:
questions.subject: Meaning, Characteristics, Stress and Defence Mechanisms
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KPSC / KEA / TET). Selye also distinguished eustress (helpful stress) from distress.

questions.question: A conflict in which a person must choose between two equally attractive goals is called:
questions.subject: Meaning, Characteristics, Stress and Defence Mechanisms
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KPSC / KEA / TET). Kurt Lewin classified conflicts this way.

questions.question: Frustration arises when:

options.B: A person's effort to reach a goal is blocked

questions.subject: Meaning, Characteristics, Stress and Defence Mechanisms
questions.explanation: Repeated frustration can lead to aggression or withdrawal.

questions.question: A student who fails an exam says, 'The paper was unfair anyway.' This defence mechanism is:
questions.subject: Meaning, Characteristics, Stress and Defence Mechanisms
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KPSC / KEA / TET). It gives a reasonable-sounding excuse ('sour grapes').

questions.question: Directing an unacceptable impulse, such as aggression, into a socially valued activity such as boxing or debating is:
questions.subject: Meaning, Characteristics, Stress and Defence Mechanisms
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KPSC / KEA / TET). Freud considered sublimation the healthiest defence mechanism.

questions.question: Attributing one's own unacceptable feelings or faults to others is called:
questions.subject: Meaning, Characteristics, Stress and Defence Mechanisms
questions.explanation: e.g. a dishonest person thinking everyone cheats.

questions.question: A man scolded by his boss comes home and shouts at his child. This is:
questions.subject: Meaning, Characteristics, Stress and Defence Mechanisms
questions.explanation: The feeling is shifted to a safer target.

questions.question: A seven-year-old starts sucking his thumb again after a baby sister is born. This is:
questions.subject: Meaning, Characteristics, Stress and Defence Mechanisms
questions.explanation: Returning to behaviour of an earlier stage.

questions.question: World Mental Health Day is observed every year on:
questions.subject: Meaning, Characteristics, Stress and Defence Mechanisms
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KPSC / KEA / TET). 7 April is World Health Day; 21 June is International Yoga Day.

questions.question: India's Mental Healthcare Act, 2017:

options.B: Gives a right to mental healthcare and effectively decriminalises attempted suicide

questions.subject: Meaning, Characteristics, Stress and Defence Mechanisms
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KPSC / KEA / TET). The National Mental Health Programme began in 1982; Tele-MANAS (helpline 14416) started in 2022.

questions.question: A teacher can best promote pupils' mental health by:

options.C: Creating a friendly, fearless classroom, praising effort and guiding pupils with problems

questions.subject: Meaning, Characteristics, Stress and Defence Mechanisms
questions.explanation: The school is second only to the home in shaping mental health.

questions.question:
Match the defence mechanism with the example:
a. Rationalisation
b. Projection
c. Displacement
d. Compensation

1. A weak student excels in sports
2. Blaming others for one's own dishonesty
3. Shouting at a younger brother after a scolding
4. 'The grapes are sour anyway'
questions.subject: Meaning, Characteristics, Stress and Defence Mechanisms
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KPSC / KEA / TET). Defence-mechanism matching is common in TET and KSET Education papers.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. Mental health is influenced by heredity, family, school and society.
II. A mentally healthy person never feels stress.
Which is/are correct?
questions.subject: Meaning, Characteristics, Stress and Defence Mechanisms
questions.explanation: Mentally healthy people feel stress but cope with it.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Defence mechanisms protect a person from anxiety.
Reason (R): They distort or deny reality, usually without the person being aware of it.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Meaning, Characteristics, Stress and Defence Mechanisms
questions.explanation: Freud and Anna Freud described them as unconscious processes; overuse becomes unhealthy.

questions.question: The main difference between psychosis and neurosis is that in psychosis:

options.A: The person loses contact with reality (e.g. hallucinations, delusions)
options.B: The person keeps full insight into the problem

questions.subject: Mental Disorders, Prevention and Treatment
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KPSC / KEA / TET). In neurosis (anxiety-based disorders) the person keeps contact with reality.

questions.question: Hearing voices that are not there is an example of a:
questions.subject: Mental Disorders, Prevention and Treatment
questions.explanation: A delusion is a fixed false belief.

questions.question: Schizophrenia is a mental disorder marked mainly by:

options.B: Disturbed thinking, hallucinations, delusions and withdrawal from reality

questions.subject: Mental Disorders, Prevention and Treatment
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KPSC / KEA / TET). It is a psychotic disorder.

questions.question: Persistent sadness, loss of interest, poor sleep and feelings of worthlessness are typical of:
questions.subject: Mental Disorders, Prevention and Treatment
questions.explanation: Depression is one of the leading causes of disability worldwide (WHO).

questions.question: A disorder in which periods of extreme elation (mania) alternate with periods of depression is:
questions.subject: Mental Disorders, Prevention and Treatment
questions.explanation: It was earlier called manic-depressive psychosis.

questions.question: An intense, irrational fear of a specific object or situation is a:
questions.subject: Mental Disorders, Prevention and Treatment
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KPSC / KEA / TET). e.g. acrophobia (heights), claustrophobia (closed spaces).

questions.question: Repeated unwanted thoughts with urges to perform acts such as checking or hand-washing again and again indicate:
questions.subject: Mental Disorders, Prevention and Treatment
questions.explanation: Obsessions are thoughts; compulsions are acts.

questions.question: A child who is constantly restless, impulsive and unable to sustain attention may have:
questions.subject: Mental Disorders, Prevention and Treatment
questions.explanation: Teachers should refer such children for assessment and use structured routines.

questions.question: Early detection and prompt treatment of a mental disorder is which level of prevention?
questions.subject: Mental Disorders, Prevention and Treatment
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KPSC / KEA / TET). Primary prevention stops a disorder from arising; tertiary prevention is rehabilitation.

questions.question: Client-centred (person-centred) therapy was developed by:
questions.subject: Mental Disorders, Prevention and Treatment
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KPSC / KEA / TET). It stresses empathy, genuineness and unconditional positive regard.

questions.question: Psychoanalysis, using free association and dream analysis, was developed by:
questions.subject: Mental Disorders, Prevention and Treatment
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KPSC / KEA / TET). It seeks to bring repressed conflicts into awareness.

questions.question: Cognitive behaviour therapy (CBT) mainly works by:

options.A: Identifying and changing faulty thinking patterns and behaviours

questions.subject: Mental Disorders, Prevention and Treatment
questions.explanation: Aaron Beck developed cognitive therapy; Albert Ellis developed REBT.

questions.question: The National Institute of Mental Health and Neuro-Sciences (NIMHANS) is located in:
questions.subject: Mental Disorders, Prevention and Treatment
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KPSC / KEA / TET). It is an Institute of National Importance.

questions.question: Which of these helps promote mental health in daily life?

options.C: Regular exercise, yoga and meditation, enough sleep and supportive relationships

questions.subject: Mental Disorders, Prevention and Treatment
questions.explanation: WHO also stresses avoiding harmful use of alcohol and drugs.

questions.question: Dependence on alcohol or drugs that harms a person's health and social life is called:
questions.subject: Mental Disorders, Prevention and Treatment
questions.explanation: Tobacco, alcohol and drug use are major risks for mental and physical health.

questions.question:
Match the phobia with its object of fear:
a. Acrophobia
b. Claustrophobia
c. Hydrophobia
d. Agoraphobia

1. Closed spaces
2. Water
3. Heights
4. Open or crowded public places
questions.subject: Mental Disorders, Prevention and Treatment
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KPSC / KEA / TET). Phobia matching appears in GK and Education papers.

questions.question:
Match the therapy with its originator:
a. Psychoanalysis
b. Client-centred therapy
c. Cognitive therapy
d. Behaviour therapy (systematic desensitisation)

1. Joseph Wolpe
2. Aaron Beck
3. Sigmund Freud
4. Carl Rogers
questions.subject: Mental Disorders, Prevention and Treatment
questions.explanation: Systematic desensitisation is widely used to treat phobias.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. In psychosis, the person often loses contact with reality.
II. Mental illness is always caused by weak will power.
Which is/are correct?
questions.subject: Mental Disorders, Prevention and Treatment
questions.explanation: Mental illnesses have biological, psychological and social causes.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Stigma prevents many people from seeking help for mental illness.
Reason (R): Mental illness is often wrongly seen as a personal weakness or something shameful.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Mental Disorders, Prevention and Treatment
questions.explanation: Awareness campaigns aim to reduce this stigma.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) is the first treatment for every mild mental problem.
Reason (R): ECT is used in some cases of severe depression that do not respond to other treatment.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Mental Disorders, Prevention and Treatment
questions.explanation: ECT is reserved for severe cases, so A is false.

sets.name: 1 · Nutrients, Dietary Requirements and Balanced Diet

questions.question: The nutrient which is helpful for our body growth is
questions.subject: Nutrients, Dietary Requirements and Balanced Diet
questions.explanation: Proteins are body-building foods – they make and repair tissues. Carbohydrates and fats give energy; vitamins protect. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: Which vitamin is enriched in outer surface of rice?
questions.subject: Nutrients, Dietary Requirements and Balanced Diet
questions.explanation: The bran layer of rice is rich in B vitamins, especially thiamine (B1); polishing removes it, which is why polished-rice diets caused beriberi. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: This is not an example for denatured protein.
questions.subject: Nutrients, Dietary Requirements and Balanced Diet
questions.explanation: Starch is a carbohydrate, not a protein. Heat (boiled egg), acid (curdling of milk) and clumping (insulin) denature proteins. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)
questions.source: Legislative Council 2024 Asst/Computer Operator P1 · Q48

questions.question: A balanced diet is one that:

options.C: Has equal amounts of every food
options.D: Contains all nutrients in the right amounts for the body's needs, along with roughage and water

questions.subject: Nutrients, Dietary Requirements and Balanced Diet
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KPSC / KEA / TET). Needs vary with age, sex, body size, activity and physiological state (pregnancy, lactation).

questions.question: Carbohydrates and fats are known as:
questions.subject: Nutrients, Dietary Requirements and Balanced Diet
questions.explanation: Proteins are body-building foods; vitamins and minerals are protective foods.

questions.question: 1 gram of carbohydrate, protein and fat gives about ____ kcal of energy respectively.
questions.subject: Nutrients, Dietary Requirements and Balanced Diet
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KPSC / KEA / TET). Fat is the most concentrated source of energy.

questions.question: Which of the following is a fat-soluble vitamin?
questions.subject: Nutrients, Dietary Requirements and Balanced Diet
questions.explanation: Fat-soluble: A, D, E, K. Water-soluble: B-complex and C.

questions.question: Dietary fibre (roughage) mainly helps to:

options.D: Prevent constipation and aid bowel movement

questions.subject: Nutrients, Dietary Requirements and Balanced Diet
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KPSC / KEA / TET). Sources: whole grains, pulses, fruits and leafy vegetables.

questions.question: The richest natural source of vitamin C among these is:
questions.subject: Nutrients, Dietary Requirements and Balanced Diet
questions.explanation: Citrus fruits and guava are also rich sources; vitamin C is lost on prolonged cooking.

questions.question: The 'sunshine vitamin', made in the skin when it is exposed to sunlight, is:
questions.subject: Nutrients, Dietary Requirements and Balanced Diet
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KPSC / KEA / TET). It helps the absorption of calcium and phosphorus.

questions.question: Which mineral is needed for the formation of haemoglobin?
questions.subject: Nutrients, Dietary Requirements and Balanced Diet
questions.explanation: Green leafy vegetables, jaggery, ragi and meat are good sources.

questions.question: According to ICMR–NIN's 'My Plate for the Day', the largest share of a day's food should come from:

options.C: Vegetables and fruits together with cereals

questions.subject: Nutrients, Dietary Requirements and Balanced Diet
questions.explanation: About half the plate should be vegetables and fruits; cereals, pulses/meat, milk and nuts make up the rest.

questions.question: Which food group is a good source of complete (first-class) protein?
questions.subject: Nutrients, Dietary Requirements and Balanced Diet
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KPSC / KEA / TET). A cereal–pulse combination (e.g. rice and dal) also gives good-quality protein for vegetarians.

questions.question: Iodine is added to common salt mainly to prevent:
questions.subject: Nutrients, Dietary Requirements and Balanced Diet
questions.explanation: India's universal salt iodisation began under the National Goitre Control Programme (1962).

questions.question: The amount of energy a person needs depends mainly on:

options.A: Age, sex, body weight and physical activity
options.B: Only the colour of the skin

questions.subject: Nutrients, Dietary Requirements and Balanced Diet
questions.explanation: A heavy worker needs much more energy than a sedentary person.

questions.question: Water is considered an essential part of the diet because it:

options.C: Regulates body temperature and carries nutrients and wastes

questions.subject: Nutrients, Dietary Requirements and Balanced Diet
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KPSC / KEA / TET). About 60% of an adult's body weight is water.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. Vitamins are needed in small amounts but are essential.
II. Excess intake of fat-soluble vitamins can be harmful because they are stored in the body.
questions.subject: Nutrients, Dietary Requirements and Balanced Diet
questions.explanation: Too much vitamin A or D, for example, causes toxicity (hypervitaminosis).

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Pregnant and lactating women need extra protein, iron and calcium.
Reason (R): Their bodies support the growth of the baby and the production of milk.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Nutrients, Dietary Requirements and Balanced Diet
questions.explanation: Iron–folic acid supplements are given under Anaemia Mukt Bharat.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Polished rice is more nutritious than unpolished rice.
Reason (R): Polishing removes the bran layer of rice.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Nutrients, Dietary Requirements and Balanced Diet
questions.explanation: Removing the bran loses B vitamins, fibre and minerals, so polished rice is less nutritious.

questions.question: Ragi (finger millet) is especially valued in a Karnataka diet because it is rich in:
questions.subject: Nutrients, Dietary Requirements and Balanced Diet
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KPSC / KEA / TET). Millets were promoted during the International Year of Millets, 2023.

sets.name: 2 · Malnutrition, Deficiency Diseases and Eating Disorders

questions.question: 'Rickets' is caused due to the deficiency of which of the following Vitamins?
questions.subject: Malnutrition, Deficiency Diseases and Eating Disorders
questions.explanation: Vitamin D deficiency softens and bends children's bones (rickets); in adults it causes osteomalacia. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question:
Match the Vitamins in List-I with their deficiency diseases in List-II by choosing correct option:
List-I (Vitamins)
(a) Vitamin B12
(b) Vitamin B1
(c) Vitamin C
(d) Vitamin K
List-II (Deficiency diseases / conditions)
(i) Haemorrhages
(ii) Scurvy
(iii) Beri Beri
(iv) Pernicious Anaemia
questions.subject: Malnutrition, Deficiency Diseases and Eating Disorders
questions.explanation: B12 – pernicious anaemia; B1 (thiamine) – beriberi; C – scurvy; K – bleeding (haemorrhages), since it is needed for blood clotting. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question:
Which of the following statements about the vitamins are correct?
(a) Vitamin A and Vitamin B were discovered by Elmer McCollum.
(b) Deficiency of Vitamin D causes weak bones.
(c) Vitamin C was invented by Albert Szent-Gyorgyi.
(d) Deficiency of Vitamin B causes scurvy.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
questions.subject: Malnutrition, Deficiency Diseases and Eating Disorders
questions.explanation: Scurvy is caused by lack of vitamin C, so (d) is wrong. McCollum identified 'fat-soluble A' and 'water-soluble B'; Szent-Györgyi isolated vitamin C (Nobel 1937). (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: Malnutrition includes:

options.A: Both undernutrition and overnutrition (overweight and obesity)

questions.subject: Malnutrition, Deficiency Diseases and Eating Disorders
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KPSC / KEA / TET). WHO: malnutrition = undernutrition (wasting, stunting, underweight), micronutrient deficiencies, and overweight/obesity.

questions.question: Kwashiorkor is caused mainly by a deficiency of:
questions.subject: Malnutrition, Deficiency Diseases and Eating Disorders
questions.explanation: Signs: swollen (oedematous) belly and feet, skin and hair changes, pot belly.

questions.question: A child who is extremely thin, with 'skin and bones' appearance due to severe lack of both energy and protein, has:
questions.subject: Malnutrition, Deficiency Diseases and Eating Disorders
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KPSC / KEA / TET). Both are forms of protein-energy malnutrition (PEM).

questions.question: Low height for age, showing long-term (chronic) undernutrition, is called:
questions.subject: Malnutrition, Deficiency Diseases and Eating Disorders
questions.explanation: Wasting = low weight for height (acute); underweight = low weight for age.

questions.question: Night blindness and xerophthalmia are caused by deficiency of:
questions.subject: Malnutrition, Deficiency Diseases and Eating Disorders
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KPSC / KEA / TET). Bitot's spots on the eye are an early sign.

questions.question: The most common nutritional deficiency disorder in India, especially among women and adolescent girls, is:
questions.subject: Malnutrition, Deficiency Diseases and Eating Disorders
questions.explanation: NFHS-5 (2019–21) found over half of Indian women aged 15–49 anaemic.

questions.question: Pellagra, with the 'three Ds' – dermatitis, diarrhoea and dementia – is due to deficiency of:
questions.subject: Malnutrition, Deficiency Diseases and Eating Disorders
questions.explanation: It was common where maize (jowar) was the staple food.

questions.question: Cretinism in children and goitre are caused by the deficiency of:
questions.subject: Malnutrition, Deficiency Diseases and Eating Disorders
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KPSC / KEA / TET). Iodine is needed to make thyroid hormones.

questions.question: An eating disorder in which a person severely restricts food because of an intense fear of gaining weight is:
questions.subject: Malnutrition, Deficiency Diseases and Eating Disorders
questions.explanation: The person sees himself or herself as fat even when dangerously thin.

questions.question: Repeated episodes of overeating followed by self-induced vomiting or use of laxatives is typical of:

notes.title: Growing with self-confidence – revision sheet
notes.md:
## Growth, development, maturity
- Growth – quantitative (height, weight), stops after maturity; development – qualitative, lifelong
- Maturation – natural unfolding by heredity; learning – by practice
- Principles: continuous & orderly, cephalocaudal (head→toe), proximodistal (centre→outward), general→specific, individual differences, heredity × environment
- Adolescence (WHO) **10–19**; 'storm and stress' – G. Stanley Hall; Erikson – identity vs role confusion
- Hormones: testosterone (boys), oestrogen & progesterone (girls); menarche
- **RKSK 2014** – adolescent health programme

## Self-confidence and mental health
- Self-efficacy – **Bandura**; build it with suitable tasks, praise for effort, success experiences
- Depression – sadness/loss of interest ≥ 2 weeks; anxiety – excessive worry, restlessness
- Coping: exercise, sleep, talking, yoga, meditation, time management
- **Tele-MANAS 14416**; World Mental Health Day **10 Oct**

## Drugs
| Drug | Source | Type |
|---|---|---|
| Heroin, morphine | poppy (Papaver) | opioid – depressant |
| Charas, ganja, bhang | Cannabis sativa | cannabinoid |
| Cocaine | coca (Erythroxylum) | stimulant |
| LSD | synthetic | hallucinogen |
| Alcohol | fermentation | depressant |
| Nicotine | tobacco | stimulant, addictive |
- Tolerance, dependence, withdrawal symptoms; warning signs: falling grades, new friends, secrecy
- Laws: **NDPS Act 1985**, COTPA 2003; Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan 2020 (MoSJE), helpline **14446**
- Days: anti-drug day **26 June**; No Tobacco Day 31 May

## Sexual harassment
- **POCSO Act 2012** (amended 2019): children < 18; mandatory reporting; special courts; child's identity secret
- **POSH Act 2013**: Internal Complaints Committee (10+ employees), Local Committee (District Officer); based on **Vishaka (1997)**
- Helplines: Childline **1098**, women **181**, emergency **112**
- Good touch – bad touch: say No, go away, tell a trusted adult
